_note: V1.4c's verbs, on the SAME effects.company channel V1.4a opened and V1.4b's law reaches through an assembly. Two new ops and no new content type -- data/company-actions/ now serves three sessions the way data/diplomatic-actions/ served five. `nationalise` SETS the state's holding and is gated on `state_owned == 0` exactly as a subsidy is gated on `subsidy_active == 0`, so the only route down is the sale; `privatise` carries no terms, for the reason `withdraw_support` carries none. The price and the windfall are NOT authored here: a firm is worth PRICE_TO_OUTPUT times its own live output, so an authored figure would let this file disagree with the register about what a firm is worth. What IS authored is the political price, because tools/companies_probe.gd measured at V1.4b that this layer's own channels move growth and unemployment BELOW the opinion model's resolution -- so a rule's or a purchase's politics cannot be expressed by the measured channels and has to be written down. Weighted against opinion_constants.BLOC_SIZE rather than by eye.

actions.name: Take a Minority Stake
actions.summary: The state buys into the firm without taking it over. The holding is paid for out of borrowing, pays a share of the firm's output back to the treasury every year, and carries a share of the firm's compliance costs so its payroll does not.

actions.name: Nationalisation
actions.summary: The firm passes into public ownership outright. The state carries the whole purchase on the national debt, collects the whole dividend, and absorbs the whole of whatever the assembly's rules cost the sector.

actions.name: Privatisation
actions.summary: The state's holding is sold in full. The windfall comes off the national debt at once; the dividends, and the shelter the payroll had from the sector's rules, are gone for good.
